chunks: (2) Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn 'Uqda said: Muhammad ibn al-Mufadhdhal, Sa'dan ibn Ishaq, Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Malik, and Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Qatawani narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated to us, from Hisham ibn al-Salam, from Abu Hamza ath-Thimali, from Abu Ishaq as-Subay'i, who said: I heard one of the trusted companions of the Commander of the Faithful saying: The Commander of the Faithful said in a long sermon he delivered in Kufa, mentioning it:

"O Allah, it is necessary for You to have authorities on Your earth, one authority after another, over Your creation, guiding them to Your religion and teaching them Your knowledge, so that the followers of Your guardians do not become divided. They are either apparent but not obeyed, or concealed, fearful, and awaiting. If their persons are absent from people during their truce in the state of untruth, their scattered knowledge will not be absent knowledge will not be absent from them. Their principles are fixed in the hearts of the believers, and they act upon them. They find comfort in what the liars find alienating and what the extravagant regarding Allah reject. Speech that is measured without a price; if there were one who hears it with his mind, recognizes it, believes in it, and follows it, and adopts its path and succeeds thereby? Then he said: Who is this? And this is why knowledge is lost because it finds no bearers to preserve it and transmit it as they heard it from the scholars."

"O Allah, and I know well that knowledge is not entirely lost nor its means cut off, for You do not leave Your earth without an authority over Your creation, either apparent and obeyed, or concealed and submerged, not obeyed, so that Your proof is not invalidated and Your friends do not go astray after You have guided them."
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the preservation of knowledge and the role of authorities in the earth?
ai.summary: This passage from Al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the Shia doctrine of *Hujjah* (divine proof), emphasizing that God never leaves the earth without an authority, whether manifest and obeyed or hidden and concealed. It underscores the continuity of guidance through the preservation of knowledge in the hearts of believers, ensuring that the lineage of divine instruction remains unbroken even during periods of political dominance by falsehood.
